overview: This Senate resolution honors the 49 people killed and dozens wounded in the June 12, 2016, shooting at the Pulse nightclub in Orlando, Florida, carried out by a gunman inspired by the Islamic State terrorist group. It describes the attack as an attack on the LGBTQ community, the Hispanic community, Orlando, Florida, and the nation, and marks nine years since it happened. The resolution offers condolences to victims' families, honors the survivors, pledges to stand against terrorism and hate, and thanks the police and emergency medical workers who responded. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on June 18, 2025.
for: Supporters say formally remembering the victims and survivors keeps the memory of one of the deadliest mass shootings in U.S. history alive and shows national solidarity with the communities targeted.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, including anything aimed at preventing similar attacks.
